questions.stem: After vigorous exercise, a person continues to breathe heavily. What is the body doing during this recovery period?

options.text: Repaying the oxygen debt by breaking down lactic acid in the liver
Storing extra oxygen in the bones for later use
Producing more lactic acid to fuel the muscles

questions.explanation: After exercise, the body must repay the oxygen debt. Extra oxygen taken in through continued heavy breathing is used to break down lactic acid in the liver, converting it back to glucose. This is why breathing and heart rate remain elevated after exercise stops.
